chapters.summary: In Meldan, Gladias, an Acolyte of the Order of Steering, casts a randomly assigned quadratic vote on a building's aesthetics tax, then attends a Dreadknot metal concert to judge which tier of the social-impact tax rubric the band belongs in; despite Emerald's unreliable analysis and the risk to his Acolyte prediction score, he votes Tier 3. Someone in the crowd shouts that he is an Order member, and he escapes by tricking a man into looking away, snatching his hand device, wiping its recent photos and videos, and fleeing while a stranger acts as a decoy. At home with Seila and the four children (Lily is upset about a failed history exam), the family eats takeout before the kids leave in four days for six months with their co-family, and Seila plans a trip to Freetown to see Jahn. During dinner an anonymous, reputation-verified sender messages Gladias saying they saw him at the concert and know he is in the Order, will not report him for the bounty, but have a request.

In Pafogai Du, Zei tells his friend Fin he placed third in a Minpentai game, and the two head to a class of the Decentralized University (DU), whose location is only revealed by encrypted broadcast and is changed again at the last minute. Zei impresses the instructor by explaining why time-reversible physics means entropy cannot be reversed, but an explosion in the room where the class was originally scheduled shakes their room, and debris breaks Zei's arm. Afterward the instructor explains that the Arctic Empire aims to keep Dzego's industry and technology permanently weak, while Dzego answers with its 'grow roots, no head' strategy of distributed manufacturing and anonymous cryptographic coordination, and he warns that the attacks will likely worsen. Fin and Zei respond with the defiant vow that Dzego will rise again.

Walking through Meldan, Gladias passes an Arctic Empire recruitment poster signed by its consul, Lord Ephelion, and meets his friend and fellow Order member Mov, who gives him a fresh privacy robe, explains a fight over taxing Bluewhale's newly closed API, and plans to shadow the meeting with the anonymous stranger. Gladias enters the walled enclave of Greater Plum Harbor, overhearing locals debate how it is penalized on land tax, and in a hidden booth meets the stranger, who names himself Delwart. Delwart praises Gladias's Tier 3 vote, argues that Steering lets prejudice override reasoned judgment, and urges him to become a Keeper instead of a Sentinel and vote to delete every rubric, part of a campaign to recruit Keepers for systemic change. He hints he can protect Gladias from those who might track him, gives him about a month to choose his track, and leaves, followed by a robed figure from the neighboring booth (later confirmed to be Mov).

Shifting between Fin and Zei in Pafogai Du, the chapter opens at a cafe where Zei studies Minpentai countermeasures, noting that time-reversible rules mean no defense is invincible, and Fin explains the Bansunpei's nationwide experiment with new visual writing systems for the next version of Dzegoban. With his arm healed, Zei enters the converted mountain pyramid for the Minpentai quarter-finals, greeted by his mentor Mu and taunted by his rival Bai, then learns he has been teamed with Bai. The two barely speak until Zei, after weakening one opponent, plants Bai's symbol inside the other opponent's base, letting the pair eliminate the first opponent and force the second to resign. Mu reveals that this round's secret rule change was non-random team selection, set up as a psychological test of cooperation that they passed; Bai apologizes, and Zei half-jokingly asks her to take him (and his mother) along on her next Redshire vacation.

Zei, his mother Min, and Bai arrive in Freetown, United Cities, a sprawling, uneven city, after both teens won their semi-finals and set up a Minpentai final against each other; Zei frames the joint trip as a way out of the usual pre-match prisoner's dilemma, while Bai admits she simply wanted his company. At the Freetown Economics Institute, Zei and Bai meet Seila and her local friend Jahn and describe Dzego's struggle against Arctic attacks and its cryptographically audited surveillance cameras. The viewpoint then moves to Seila, who takes a call from Gladias; when he says someone suggested he become a Keeper, she backs the idea and proposes that one of his projects could be reshaping rubrics to help Dzego, and Gladias declares he will do it.

From a sealed, foil-lined basement, Gladias tells Mov he is choosing the Keeper track; Mov suspects Delwart's influence and reports that by tailing Delwart he found him holding a string of meetings at GPH tea shops, likely recruiting other would-be Keepers, so the two agree to play along and watch. The next day Gladias and Mov attend a citizens' assembly on public spaces run by a Herald named Alagael, where a flu alert prompts calm precautions and Mov notes that a ground-floor-use rubric is being gamed. Gladias then runs into Febric at a restaurant, covers a payment shortfall with an anonymous reputation-backed loan, and climbs to the Order's tower, where he formally confirms his application to become a Keeper.

On the eve of the Pafogai Du Minpentai final, Zei persuades Fin to skip his Bansunpei linguistics training and help build a practice pipeline, and the next day Zei, Fin, and Bai watch an Arctic strike destroy the city's largest, government-run chip fab, which Fin calls a failure of the 'no head' principle. The final's new rule gives each player a powerful AI whose reasoning the opponent can read, and Zei falls behind after taking the bait of a deliberate gap Bai left in her AI's defenses. He recovers by hiding key moves outside his AI's transcript and triggering a factory that launches attacks Bai cannot anticipate, and Bai resigns. Mu explains the priests' lesson that real power often depends on concealing one's thoughts, even from allies; the prizes include money Zei hopes to spend on a compute box for his mother, and Zei alone receives a dark purple letter marked for his eyes only, which he pockets unopened.

With Seila traveling in Iptak, Gladias listens on the autobus to a debate in which VNU president Sylka defends Veridia's broader measures of well-being and Lord Ephelion argues that only economic and technological growth compounds over time, and Gladias privately judges Ephelion a gifted demagogue. At his Parliament committee hearing, Gladias answers questions about his background, faces hostile probing from Senator Papli about being out of touch with ordinary Veridians, and wins support from Senator Ancus; the committee splits ten to ten and the Chairman's tie-breaking vote admits him to the Order. He then hurries to Vil's house to comfort Lily, who is crying over another failed test, this time in civics, and Mov calls to say he has been randomly selected to become a Herald, losing his formal power but freeing him to help Gladias, who ends the day sharing the news of his acceptance with Seila.
